item.title: AGL Jumps Most in Six Months on Strong Battery Performance
item.description: AGL Energy Ltd. shares jumped the most in six months as Australia’s largest power producer’s batteries helped offset declining wholesale electricity prices.

item.title: Qatar National Bank Tests Investor Appetite for $2 Billion Loan
item.description: Qatar National Bank is seeking a $2 billion syndicated loan, according to people familiar with the matter, in a test of whether banks, particularly from Asia, are willing to lend in the region as the US war with Iran drags on.

item.title: AI Startup Cognition in New Funding Talks at $40 Billion Value
item.description: Cognition AI is in early talks with investors for a new funding round that may boost the coding startup’s valuation by more than 50% to at least $40 billion, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: JPMorgan Boosts Singapore Stocks Target as Economic Growth Holds
item.description: JPMorgan Chase & Co. raised its target for Singapore stocks as robust economic growth and a narrowing valuation gap with developed-market peers bolster their outlook.

item.title: Indonesian Tech Firm GoTo Faces MSCI Index Exclusion in Review
item.description: GoTo Group, the Indonesian ride-hailing and food delivery platform once valued at more than $32 billion, faces the prospect of being dropped from MSCI Inc.’s indexes on Wednesday after a plunge in its share price left the stock difficult to trade.

item.title: SK Hynix, Samsung Shares Rally as Temasek Report Boosts Optimism
item.description: South Korean chipmakers rallied as risk appetite returns after last month’s rout, with a local media report of investment plans by Singapore’s Temasek Holdings Pte supporting sentiment.

item.title: China Taps Deutsche Bank as First Foreign Yuan Clearer in Europe
item.description: China has authorized Deutsche Bank AG as the first non-Chinese lender that can settle yuan transactions in Europe, expanding its clearing network to promote the currency overseas.

item.title: Korea’s 30-Year Bond Yield Hits Record on Oil, Rate Hike Bets
item.description: South Korea’s 30-year government bond yield climbed to a record, as elevated energy prices and weaker demand from life insurers intensified pressure on the debt market.

item.title: Bessent-Takaichi Split on BOJ Risks Undermining Joint Yen Rescue
item.description: Even as the US and Japan have shown rare unity in moving to strengthen the yen, a fundamental tension between Scott Bessent and Sanae Takaichi over the Bank of Japan risks undermining their efforts.

item.title: India’s Small, Mid-cap Funds Stay Hot With Investors
item.description: The smaller stocks have comfortably outpaced large caps this year.

item.title: Yen Traders Use Options for ‘Flexibility’ Into US Inflation Data
item.description: Yen traders are ramping up options market activity ahead of key US inflation data, turning to derivatives for flexibility amid a lack of consensus on the currency’s direction.

item.title: Sanrio Shares Plunge Most Since 2014 After 1Q Earnings Miss
item.description: Sanrio Co. shares tumbled as much as 20%, the most in more than 12 years, after the company’s first quarter operating income missed market estimates.

item.title: China Revives Free-Trade Zone Bond Market After 2023 Crackdown
item.description: Signs of life are returning to the Shanghai free-trade zone’s bond market, which went quiet in late 2023 after Chinese authorities clamped down on excessive borrowing by local governments.

item.title: New Zealand Prime Minister Luxon Wins Party Confidence Vote
item.description: New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon said the governing National Party has backed him to remain its leader in a confidence vote less than three months before a general election.

item.title: Rakuten Shares Fall Most in Six Months After Earnings Disappoint
item.description: Rakuten Group Inc. shares sank the most in six months after the Japanese online shopping mall operator’s quarterly operating profit missed analyst estimates.

item.title: New Katsu Curry Index Rivals Big Mac Gauge to Show How Weak Yen Really Is
item.description: A senior strategist at Bank of New York Mellon is using the price of a Japanese fast-food staple to get an accurate snapshot of the yen’s weakness as the impact of the recent intervention fades.

item.title: Jane Street Repaying $5.5 Billion Loan in Overhaul of Debt Load
item.description: Jane Street is repaying $5.5 billion of floating-rate loans as part of a broader overhaul of its $11 billion debt load.

item.title: Indonesian Bonds May Have Seen Worst of Selling, Analysts Say
item.description: Indonesia’s bond market, the worst performer in Asia, may bounce back as a new central bank chief is expected to support the currency while authorities address concerns about fiscal stability, analysts said.

item.title: From Chinamaxxing to Visa-Free Travel: Why Tourists Are Returning to China
item.description: Foreign visitors to China last year surpassed pre-pandemic levels for the first time and are continuing to rise.

item.title: Gold Advances as Traders Watch US Inflation for Rate-Hike Clues
item.description: Gold edged higher, as traders weighed prospects for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz while awaiting US inflation data that could provide fresh clues on the Federal Reserve’s interest-rate path.

item.title: China Earnings to Test Rotation From AI to Internet Stocks
item.description: A rotation into China’s biggest tech firms from AI infrastructure stocks will be tested this week as earnings are due.

item.title: China's Real Estate Market Races to Defuse a $148 Billion Time Bomb
item.description: Officials are trying to fix a problem that has hung over the sector for years.

item.title: Global Investors Favor Taiwan Over Korea Stocks After AI Selloff
item.description: Taiwanese stocks are gaining favor over South Korea’s on steadier earnings prospects, as the two AI-bellwether markets look to recover from July’s rout.

item.title: Singapore Exchange Eyes Single-Stock ETFs, Tie-Ups for Growth
item.description: Singapore Exchange Ltd. is exploring offering a broader suite of exchange-traded funds and stepping up partnerships across markets as it seeks to bolster its position as Southeast Asia’s key multi-asset exchange.

item.title: Peak Memory Fears Put Focus on Samsung, SK Hynix Cash Returns
item.description: Memory-chip makers may have found a new defense against the inevitable cooling of their boom: giving more cash back to shareholders.

item.title: Korea Sovereign Wealth Fund to Join Global Race for AI, Robotics
item.description: South Korea expects to deploy more than 1 trillion won ($707 million) of fresh capital into a new sovereign wealth fund targeting AI and other strategic industries next year, joining a global push by governments to mobilize investment and gain an edge in high-tech sectors.

item.title: Asian Stocks to Slip With US CPI, Iran in Focus: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks were poised to follow Wall Street lower as traders held back from riskier bets ahead of key inflation data and remained wary over US-Iran developments.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 12
item.description: Oil steadied after a four-day gain as traders monitored efforts for a deal that could help restore energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Blackstone Strikes $1.8 Billion Deal for Air Canada Loyalty Unit
item.description: Blackstone Inc. and a group of Canadian pension funds are buying a 25% stake in Air Canada’s Aeroplan loyalty program for C$2.5 billion ($1.8 billion).

item.title: Bitwise Cuts 14% of Jobs With Crypto Industry Under Pressure
item.description: Crypto firm Bitwise Asset Management Inc. has let go about 14% of its workforce during a prolonged slump in digital-asset prices.
